> 出生入死。生之徒十有三，死之徒十有三，人之生，動之死地，亦十有三.

Nine chapters have been about mind, perception, and how to treat others. Chapter 50 turns abruptly to the most concrete thing: the body.

And its key is in two of the plainest characters in the whole book.

## 攝 and 地

攝: 引持也 — a hand that pulls something toward itself and holds it. Not "preserve" as in keeping something in a jar; to draw in and hold.

地: 重濁陰為地 — the heavy, the turbid, the yin: what sinks down and piles into a layer.

So 善攝生 is not "good at health preservation." It is: good at drawing the living capacity back and holding it.

And 死地 is not "a place where one will die." It is the layer where the heavy has piled up and sunk.

## 出生入死

> 出生入死.

Birth is 出 — going out. Death is 入 — going in.

One road, two directions. Not two doors, and not two destinations. The chapter's whole argument depends on this: you are on the road the entire time, and the question is which way you are moving on it.

## The three in ten

生之徒十有三 — three in ten walk the road keeping life.

死之徒十有三 — three in ten are built to dissipate, and walk the road toward death.

人之生，動之死地，亦十有三 — and three in ten, alive, move themselves into the dead ground.

夫何故？以其生生之厚 — why? Because of the thickness of their living-of-life.

## 生生之厚

The second 生 is a verb: to live, to nourish, to keep alive. 生生 is the activity of keeping oneself alive, piled on top of living.

厚 is the same direction as 地: thickness, piling downward. The character family is consistent — the thing that sinks and accumulates.

So the third group dies not from neglect but from over-provisioning: the tonics, the protections, the insulation, the constant tending. Each addition thickens the layer, and the layer is 死地.

Which is the chapter's sharpest observation: the effort to secure life is itself a way of moving into the place where life is most exposed.

## 陸行不遇兕虎

The one who 善攝生 travels on land and does not meet the buffalo and the tiger; enters the army and is not touched by armor or weapons.

兕無所投其角，虎無所措其爪，兵無所容其刃 — the buffalo has nowhere to put its horn, the tiger nowhere to place its claw, the weapon nowhere to fit its blade.

## 以其無死地

> 夫何故？以其無死地.

Because there is no dead ground.

This is the line that makes the chapter more than a health tip. The protection is not armor; it is the absence of the surface that could be struck.

A claw needs a place to land. A blade needs a gap to enter. The one who has not built the thick layer has no such surface — not because he is invulnerable, but because there is nothing there to be hit.

## The two halves

Chapter 49: the sage draws inward and gives back a laugh.
Chapter 50: the same inward motion applied to the body — draw the living capacity back, and do not pile the ground that can be breached.

Both are 攝. Both are subtraction. The chapter is not about immortality; it is about not building the target.

## A test

Count the things you do purely to protect yourself — the supplements, the backups, the hedges, the pre-emptive explanations. Then ask which of them has become a layer you have to maintain. That layer is the 死地.
